supermarket.note: Napa cabbage kimchi, well fermented and sour. Fresh kimchi has no depth to give up.

general.note: Short-grain rice, cooked the day before and chilled.

optional.note: Snipped into strips for the top.

tools.name: Pan
tools.note: About 24 cm. A second small pan for the eggs saves wiping this one out.

tools.name: Scissors
tools.note: Kimchi is easier to snip than to chop.

steps.title: Cook the rice ahead
points: Cook the rice the day before and chill it uncovered.
Break it up with wet hands before you start.
Cold dry grains are the whole difference between fried rice and wet rice.

steps.title: Snip the kimchi
points: Squeeze the kimchi over a bowl and keep every drop of the juice.
Snip it into pieces about 2 cm.
The juice goes in later. It carries most of the sourness.

steps.title: Cut the pork
points: Cut the pork belly into 2 cm pieces.
Season it with the pinch of salt and pepper.

steps.title: Render the pork
points: Put the pork in the pan with the oil over medium heat.
Cook for 4 minutes, until the fat has run and the edges are browned.
Leave the fat in the pan. The kimchi cooks in it.

steps.title: Fry the kimchi
points: Add the kimchi, and the onion if you are using it.
Fry for 4 minutes over medium heat, until the edges darken and it smells sweet rather than sharp.
This step is where raw sourness turns into flavor. Do not cut it short.

steps.title: Build the paste
points: Stir in the gochujang, sugar and soy sauce.
Pour in the kimchi juice and let it cook down for 30 seconds.
The pan should look glossy, not wet.

steps.title: Add the rice
points: Tip the rice in and press it into the paste with the back of the spatula.
Toss and press for 3 minutes, until every grain has gone red.
Add the butter now if you want the sourness rounded off.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
points: In the second pan, fry the eggs in a little oil over medium-high heat.
Leave them alone until the whites are set and the edges are lacy and brown.
The yolk stays runny. It is the sauce.

steps.title: Plate and top
points: Pack the rice into a bowl and turn it out onto each plate as a dome.
Trickle the sesame oil over and scatter the nori, sesame and spring onion.
Sit the fried egg on top and break it at the table.

troubleshooting.solution: The kimchi juice went in with fresh rice, or all at once. Use day-old rice, and let the juice cook down for 30 seconds before the rice goes in.
The kimchi was not fried long enough. Four minutes over medium heat is what turns the sourness sweet. The smell tells you when it has turned.
Very old kimchi. Add another teaspoon of sugar, or a small knob of butter. Both round the edge off without making it sweet.
It went in cold and unbroken. Loosen it with wet hands first, and press it into the pan rather than stirring it.
Fresh kimchi, or not enough of it. This dish is 200 g of kimchi to 350 g of rice. Gochujang adds color and body, not sourness, so it will not rescue mild kimchi.
Bacon works and needs no extra oil. Canned tuna, drained, goes in with the rice instead of at the start. Without any of it, add a teaspoon more sesame oil at the end.
Leave it out and add a teaspoon of soy sauce. The kimchi is already carrying the chili. The dish loses some color and a little heat.
